_what: SOURCE-SIDE ingest verification for july27 — the first night in this corpus where the source hashes exist, so the first whose ingest can be verified against anything other than itself.
why_it_matters: the registry records aug09's ingest as 'local-hash verified only; no source-side hashes exist for that night — a fact about the record, not fixable after the fact'. A local re-hash proves only that a file has not changed since it was copied; it cannot detect a corruption that happened DURING the copy. july27 closes that gap for one night, so the corpus's ingest provenance is no longer uniformly caveated.
method: sha256sum -c run from sessions/july27/ against the source-side manifest, every entry, no sampling
verdict: 735 of 735 VERIFIED against source-side hashes. Zero failures, zero missing. The staged copy is bit-identical to the source.

corroborating_facts_checked_at_the_same_.frame_counts_match_the_acquisition_recor: darks 200, set-01 282, set-02 253 — set counts equal exif.frames in each set's acquisition.json
corroborating_facts_checked_at_the_same_.the_darks_MATCH_the_lights_and_are_not_b: first dark reads 3.0 s / ISO 1600 / f4.0 / 70 mm, identical to both light sets. A dark library from another night at another exposure is the common failure and it is excluded here by measurement.
corroborating_facts_checked_at_the_same_.exposure_is_the_point_of_this_night: 3.0 s against the rest of the corpus's 2.5 s — the exposure lever that makes the trail amplitude pinnable.
corroborating_facts_checked_at_the_same_.cadence_differs_and_must_be_carried_into: 6.0 s against aug06's 3.0 s, so the sky sweeps twice as far between frames. This does NOT touch the in-exposure trail, which is what the scaling test reads, but it changes drift-per-frame and the framing intersection.

what_this_does_NOT_establish: that the SOURCE was itself uncorrupted. A source-side manifest verifies the transfer, not the origin. That is the strongest claim available and it is stronger than any other night in this corpus has.
